messages:
sam: Heads-up — CI perf smoke on the release branch just flagged a 18% p95 latency regression in the runtime perf suite :eyes:
perf-ci-bot: [alert] perf/smoke/runtime_p95 increased from 120ms -> 142ms after merge sha abc1234. See: https://ci.example.com/runner/9876
maria: Oof. Which test suites are red? any kernel/batching traces?
perf-ci-bot: failing tests: batch_integration, kv_cache_sensitivity. Attached perf profile: s3://ci-artifacts/2245678901/profile.tar.gz
ryan: I pulled the profile briefly — looks like kernel selection is choosing the 'fast-attn-v2' path much more often for short sequences, but batching heuristics increased average batch size which pushes some workloads into the slow path.
devon: That matches an internal change in the batching heuristic PR (review #4206). It increased soft_max_batch by 30% under medium load to improve throughput. Might have regressed tail latency for cold KV scenarios.
sam: Can we bisect quickly to the offending commit? if it's the batching tweak we should pause the staged rollout and enable autorevert on the canary.
ryan: Running git bisect now across merge range (abc1000..abc1234). rough ETA ~20m.
infra-bot: Started reproduce job on canary cluster (canary-3). Command: `./deploy --sha abc1234 --env canary-3 --smoke`
maria: While ryan bisects, quick check: KV miss rate jumped from 2% -> 9% in the profile. If batching increased request coalescing, we may be evicting/invalidating KV entries more often — check TTL and per-batch KV attach/detach logic.
devon: Good catch. Recent kernel hint code added KV prefetch on batch start; if prefetch logic created transient map keys, the eviction churn could spike miss rate. I'll instrument more counters.
ryan: Bisect result: blame commit abc1198 (author: devon) — batching heuristic change. Reproducer traces attached.
sam: OK — recommended action? revert or patch? we have a running canary A/B: 10% variant B with new batching.
maria: My suggestion: pause A/B rollout immediately. Route new requests to variant A until we ship a patch. Also enable the auto-rollback gate if SLO breach persists > 5 minutes.
perf-ci-bot: Gate triggered: runtime_p95 > 140ms for 5m. Auto-rollback policy: disabled for manual rollouts, enabled for staged by default.
sam: @devon can you push a minimal patch to restore previous soft_max_batch and disable KV prefetch by default? we can re-run canary with instrumented counters.
devon: On it — will open PR with revert of soft_max_batch bump + feature flag for kv-prefetch off. small change, ~15 lines.
ryan: Also adding a canary guard to the rollout controller: require both synthetic-slo and real-traffic-slo to be green. synthetic alone isn't sufficient for KV churn detection.
maria: Agree. We should add a sampling rule: for first 30m of A/B, sample 10% of requests for KV probes and track per-route kv_miss_rate. If kv_miss_rate delta > 3% vs baseline, auto-pause rollout.
sam: Good. Also add CI check that runs the perf smoke suite with reduced batching to catch this earlier.
infra-bot: Deploy job queued: patch-pr-4290 -> canary-3, expected finish 2245679480.
perf-ci-bot: After patch test run: runtime_p95 dropped to 123ms, kv_miss_rate back to 2.1%.
maria: Nice. Reopen A/B only after we bake the sampling guard and add rollback policy to the controller.
devon: Will add rollout controller flag + tests. ETA 2 business days.
sam: Summary: bisected to batching heuristic change (abc1198), reverted the throughput bump, disabled kv-prefetch, paused A/B rollout, added canary guard tasks (synthetic+real SLOs + kv sampling) and CI perf smoke addition. Thanks team :pray:
